llm.summary: The skill's actions match its described purpose (booking SF weekend cleanings) but there are a few inconsistencies and provenance/privacy risks you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required binary (claw-cleaning), and the runtime instructions all align: the skill runs a CLI to check availability and create bookings. However the registry metadata at the top reported 'No install spec' while SKILL.md contains install metadata (an npm install entry); confirm which install mechanism the platform will actually use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions legitimately call the claw-cleaning CLI and collect booking data (address, name, email, payment preference). Two issues: (1) SKILL.md references an optional environment variable CLAW_CLEANING_SERVER_URL that is not declared in the registry requires.env — instructions referencing undeclared env vars should be verified; (2) the skill handles PII and payment flows (Stripe checkout URLs, saved cards) and relies on the agent to follow safety rules (explicit confirmation before booking). Those safety rules are textual only and not enforced by the platform.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill expects an npm package 'claw-cleaning' (metadata in SKILL.md). npm installs are a moderate-risk install mechanism (remote code runs on the agent host). There is no homepage and the package/owner are unknown in the provided registry data — you should inspect the npm package source and its publisher before allowing automatic installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required credentials and does not request unrelated secrets. It does send user-provided PII (addresses, names, emails) and payment state to a remote service (https://claw.cleaning and Stripe URLs) which is expected for a booking flow but worth noting for privacy and compliance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (platform default). Because the skill performs networked booking operations and payment flows, autonomous invocation combined with the reliance on textual safety rules means the agent could, if misconfigured or coerced, initiate bookings or reveal payment links; verify the agent enforces confirmation before performing irreversible actions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: (1) Confirm whether the platform will auto-install the npm package declared inside SKILL.md (there's a mismatch with registry metadata). (2) Inspect the 'claw-cleaning' npm package and its publisher (no homepage/owner info provided here). (3) Be aware the skill will collect and transmit PII (addresses, emails, names) and will surface Stripe payment URLs and saved-card behavior — ensure this matches your privacy policy and user consent. (4) Verify the agent actually enforces the SKILL.md safety rule requiring explicit user confirmation before running claw-cleaning book (the rule is textual only). (5) If you run a staging instance, confirm how CLAW_CLEANING_SERVER_URL is handled and that it is not left pointing to a malicious endpoint. If you cannot validate the npm package provenance or confirm the platform's install behavior, treat this skill as higher risk and avoid automatic installation.
